base_note: V128 starts from grok's V127 tree byte-for-byte. That tree is the one that returned Plugin Check ERRORS: 0 on the Captain's machine, so it is the only sane base. The 6 files that differed between the claude-opus-5 and grok-4-6 candidate trees were synced TO grok's version first, including grok's correct trajectory regex and grok's admin/settings.php (which is not a regression: line 320 already gates the page on can_access_flow_admin(), and line 323 is a narrower gate for the administration tab only).
changes_from_v127: includes/sso/class-oauth2-handler.php: added 'use WP_REST_Request; use WP_REST_Response;'. Under 'namespace FLOSC\SSO' the docblocks at 160/161/255/737 resolved to FLOSC\SSO\WP_REST_Request, which does not exist. Executable code already used the global correctly; this makes the docblocks resolve. Zero behaviour change.
includes/sso/class-sso-provider-base.php and the 5 provider classes: added 'use WP_Error;' for the same reason. Zero behaviour change.

includes/class-flosc-concierge.php: password_matches() docblock claimed 'a constant-time compare'. The code is mb_stripos(), which is a SUBSTRING search, so it is neither an equality check nor constant-time. The comment now states what the code does, including that 'the password is monki' passes. CODE NOT CHANGED -- tightening a live gate is the Captain's call, not mine. See open_decisions.

build-dist-zip.sh: added an rsync->tar staging fallback. rsync is absent from minimal containers, and without it the build refused outright ('rsync: command not found'), which took 8 zip-content gates from runnable to unrunnable. On a machine with rsync, behaviour is byte-identical.

also_fixed_outside_the_shipped_tree: includes/class-flosc-trajectory.php (repo ROOT copy, line 428): preg_replace('#[/?#].*$#', ...) -- the '#' inside the character class closes the pattern at '#[/?' and ']' becomes an invalid modifier. what_this_candidate_does_NOT_prove: Plugin Check was NOT run here -- wp-cli and Docker are not in this container. The Captain's own V127 run produced 'ERRORS: 0'; V128 changes 5 files, of which 7 edits are use-statements and docblocks with zero runtime effect, and one is a build-script fallback that does not ship. Plugin Check must still be re-run on this exact zip.
No interactive functionality was exercised. Chat continuity, logging, AI personality creation and selection, and Catalogs have NO evidence from this session. Nobody clicked anything.
No starter pack was installed and used. 4 pack.json ship and the zip passes packaging gates, but 'does not break the plugin when put into use' is untested.

PHPStan level 5 was not run here (no phpstan in this container). The Captain's V127 run reported 729 errors; the SSO use-statements added here should remove roughly 45 of them, which is a PREDICTION, not a measurement.

Semgrep was not run here. Of the 8 findings in the V127 run, the 3 new tainted-filename hits (class-flosc-framework.php:3526, :3587, :13771) were read individually and are FALSE POSITIVES: site 1 has sanitize_file_name + a nonce bound to the filename + manage_options; site 2 has sanitize_file_name + nonce + manage_options; site 3 pins the name with an anchored allowlist /^phrase-\d+\.(webm|mp4|m4a|ogg|wav)$/ before building the path AND an HMAC over all four values compared with hash_equals. Semgrep's rule is dataflow-based and does not model preg_match guards.
open_decisions_for_the_captain: password_matches() uses mb_stripos(), so any reply CONTAINING the password opens the gate. The docblock now says so honestly. Making it a real equality check is one line -- replace the return with: return '' !== $given && hash_equals( $expected, $given ); -- which would also make a 'constant-time' claim true. It TIGHTENS a live gate, so it is not mine to decide.

verify-flosc.sh reports 'exit 0' over red blocks. It is NOT in this repo -- it lives only on the Captain's machine, so it could not be fixed from here. testing-environment/flosc-test, which IS in the repo, was inspected and is already correct: foot() sets RC=1 on any non-zero code, notrun() sets RC=1, and the dispatcher ends in 'exit $RC'. The swallowing is in the outer script.
